$comment: Hand-authored seed transfer items (no AI) for the Wednesday review loop. Each item tests one concept at a ladder level: L0 definition, L1 paraphrase, L2 single-concept application, L3 novel application, L4 multi-concept reasoning, L5 full passage. 'answer' is the index into 'choices'. 'source_ref' names the source the item is grounded in. ai_generated=false for all seed items; AI-generated items (Friday) follow the same schema with ai_generated=true and a source_ref to a named chapter. Difficulty 'b' is the item difficulty used by the Elo/IRT transfer model (higher = harder), frozen after authoring per PRD risk mitigation.

choices: the breakdown of glucose to two molecules of pyruvate
the synthesis of glucose from lactate
the oxidation of fatty acids to acetyl-CoA
the storage of glucose as glycogen

items.stem: Which statement describes the same idea as 'glycolysis has a net yield of 2 ATP per glucose'?
choices: Glycolysis consumes 2 ATP and produces 4 ATP
Glycolysis produces 2 ATP and consumes 4 ATP
Glycolysis neither makes nor uses ATP
Glycolysis requires oxygen to make ATP

items.stem: A muscle cell is rapidly contracting with insufficient oxygen. Which process regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue?
During prolonged fasting, blood glucagon rises. In hepatocytes this most directly causes:
Glucagon raises hepatic cAMP, activating PKA. PKA simultaneously phosphorylates the bifunctional enzyme PFK-2/FBPase-2. The net effect on fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and on flux is:
choices: F2,6BP falls; glycolysis slows and gluconeogenesis speeds up

items.stem: PASSAGE: A researcher infuses glucagon into a fasting subject and measures a rapid rise in hepatic glucose output, then a slower sustained component. Blocking glycogen phosphorylase abolishes the rapid component but not the sustained one. QUESTION: The sustained component is best explained by:
choices: gluconeogenesis from amino acids and glycerol

items.stem: The Michaelis constant Km is defined as:
choices: the substrate concentration at half of Vmax
the rate constant for product release
the enzyme concentration at half saturation

items.stem: Saying 'a lower Km means higher affinity' is equivalent to:
choices: less substrate is needed to reach half-maximal rate
more substrate is needed to reach Vmax

items.stem: An inhibitor increases the apparent Km but leaves Vmax unchanged. This is:
On a Lineweaver-Burk plot, two lines intersect on the y-axis but have different slopes. The drug responsible most likely acts as a:
An allosteric enzyme shows a sigmoidal v-vs-[S] curve. Adding a positive effector shifts the curve left. Compared to Michaelis-Menten kinetics, the key difference and the effect of the effector are:
choices: cooperativity makes the curve sigmoidal; the effector lowers apparent K0.5
no cooperativity; the effector raises Vmax only
cooperativity is absent; the effector denatures the enzyme
the curve is hyperbolic; the effector has no effect

items.stem: PASSAGE: An assay of enzyme E shows Vmax = 100 with substrate alone. Adding compound X gives the same Vmax but doubles Km. Adding compound Y lowers both Vmax and Km proportionally. QUESTION: X and Y are, respectively:
A buffer is best defined as a solution that:
choices: resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added

items.stem: Restating Henderson-Hasselbalch, a buffer has maximum capacity when:
choices: pH equals pKa (equal amounts of acid and conjugate base)

items.stem: You need a buffer at pH 4.7. Which weak acid (given its pKa) is the best choice?
Blood plasma is buffered near pH 7.4 by the bicarbonate system (pKa 6.1). Despite pH being more than 1 unit above pKa, the system works well in vivo because:
choices: CO2 is continuously removed by the lungs, keeping the system open
the pKa is actually 7.4 in plasma

items.stem: A patient hyperventilates, lowering arterial CO2. Using the bicarbonate buffer equation, the expected acid-base change and the kidney's compensatory response are:

PASSAGE: A 0.1 M solution of a weak acid HA is titrated with NaOH. At the half-equivalence point the pH reads 4.8; at the equivalence point the pH is 8.9. QUESTION: The pKa of HA and the reason the equivalence-point pH exceeds 7 are:
choices: pKa 4.8; the conjugate base A- hydrolyzes to give a basic solution
pKa 4.8; excess NaOH dominates regardless of A-
